reason: The plugin is primarily a speech interaction utility for DSH web conversations, combining in-page text-to-speech playback and voice-to-text input. Evidence in the README and package metadata shows user-facing controls for announcements, ASR mic input, hotkeys, and settings, with networked external TTS/ASR engines, so it is best classified as a media-oriented web utility with medium interaction risk.

summaries.zh: DSH Web 语音套件插件，用于在会话界面中进行语音播报与语音转文字输入，支持热键控制、可选自动发送和语音参数设置。
summaries.en: A DSH web plugin for speech interaction in chat, enabling in-page voice playback and microphone-to-text input with configurable hotkeys and optional auto-send behavior.

capabilities: In-browser text-to-speech playback of reply content via configurable engines
Microphone recording and streaming transcription into the chat input box
Hotkey-triggered toggle/push-to-talk control flow with optional auto-send
Local browser preference storage and external network-based service integration

reasons.code: README states the plugin can read each reply in-page via a per-message button and auto-announce toggle in the conversation UI.
README documents a speech pipeline from browser PCM capture through plugin WebSocket to Aliyun Bailian/Volcengine realtime ASR, then inserting text into the composer.

README mentions optional API keys for ASR services and selectable engines (dashscope/volcengine) plus hotkey (Alt+Q) and hold-to-talk behavior, indicating external service dependence and user credential usage.
package.json declares a web DSH client plugin with websocket-related dependency (`ws`) and platform binding to web, matching browser-side integration with networked voice services.
